# BAD-071 — Admin loose ends: delete the five vestigial banners, document the client/server boundary in admin/CLAUDE.md, and clear the one standing lint warning

## Brief
One pass over the admin dashboard's loose ends, merged from BAD-071, BAD-081 and BAD-083 (2026-09-16 triage). Three distinct deliverables that share a PR because they share a test-and-lint run, not because they are the same edit — keep all three, none is a subset of another. All verified present on main e9f8709.

**1. Five vestigial section banners (was BAD-071).** The BAD-054 spike's §4 ranges included each declaration's leading comments, so slicing carried `page.tsx`'s old section dividers into the new files, where they now divide nothing — a single file's table of contents sitting at the top of single-purpose modules. Present today: `_lib/flags-or-null.ts:5` ("---- user"), `_components/LogsTab.tsx:6` ("---- logs"), `_components/UsageTab.tsx:9` ("---- usage"), and `_components/UserTab.tsx:92` ("---- profile") plus `:94` ("---- bits"), the last two mid-file and called "leftover" by the spike itself. They were deliberately not dropped inside BAD-054: `verify-moves.cjs` reports every comment that disappears, and deleting them would have replaced step 4's single required "OK: 20 statements" line with COMMENT LOST output, which that brief treats as a failure. That constraint is gone now that PR 2 has landed. Five one-line deletions, no code touched.

**2. `admin/CLAUDE.md` documents the pool rule but not the client/server boundary (was BAD-081).** Its two bullets both end by naming the test that pins them (`test/server/admin-pool.test.mjs`). The client/server boundary now has three enforced rules across two test files — `admin-client-boundary.test.mjs` (no server module reads a plain value out of a `'use client'` module; a library module that pulls server code declares `import 'server-only'`; every leaf behind a server-only barrel declares it) and `admin-actions-boundary.test.mjs` (every `'use server'` export opens with `requireAdmin`; the support leaves under `lib/actions/` open with the guard) — and `admin/CLAUDE.md` mentions none of it across its 54 lines. Confirmed: grep for `server-only|use client|use server|boundary` returns nothing; the only hit anywhere in admin prose is `README.md:316`, about env accessors. A developer adding a module under `admin/src/lib/` learns the rule by tripping a test instead of by reading the area's own file. The part hardest to guess is which modules deliberately carry NO guard and why (`action-state`, `cookies`, `env`, `format`, `platforms`; `installbase`, `retention`, `segments`; the five `'use server'` leaves) — 31 files declare the guard and 8 explain at length why they do not.

**3. The one standing lint warning (was BAD-083).** `npm run lint` in `admin/` has exactly one: `admin/src/components/Rail.tsx:102`, `@next/next/no-location-assign-relative-destination`, for `window.location.href = '/login'` at the end of `signOut`. Read the site before changing it. The rule's usual argument — that a full page load throws away the client router's cache and prefetch — is the point here, not the cost: `signOut` has just POSTed to `/api/auth/signout` to clear the cookie, and a `router.push()` would carry the RSC cache of an authenticated session across the boundary unless paired with `router.refresh()`. The comment two lines above already says the route handler answers JSON rather than a redirect so the navigation happens client-side. So this is probably a disable comment carrying that reasoning, not a code change — but confirm that reading against how the rest of the dashboard signs out, and if `router.push()` plus `router.refresh()` is genuinely equivalent, say why. Either way `npm run lint` should end at zero problems, so the next real warning is visible.

Verification: `npm run lint` in `admin/` ends at zero problems; `npm test` covers the boundary tests; the banner deletions touch no code.
